finding.claim: /checkout computes the charge from client-supplied price and qty with no server-side catalog lookup or validation. An attacker can set arbitrary prices (for example 0.01) to buy at any price, or send negative price or qty values to get a zero or negative total, which may become a refund or credit.

trace.note: POST /checkout handler; no validation middleware visible in this file
total = sum(i.price * i.qty) using raw client values
total passed directly to the payment charge
total echoed back to the client

finding.guards_checked: No catalog price lookup, no numeric, sign or integer checks on price or qty, and no minimum-total check in cart.js. The only router in the repo is this file, so any upstream body-validation middleware cannot be ruled out, but none is visible. The newer /checkout-v2 route uses the catalog, which suggests /checkout is a legacy route that was left live.

verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums raw req.body.items price*qty and cart.js:6 passes it to req.payments.charge, with no validation in the file, while the /checkout-v2 handler (cart.js:13-14) shows the catalog lookup and qty clamp that /checkout lacks. Only cart.js exists in the repo, so any upstream middleware cannot be seen, and the attacker only needs to be an authenticated user (req.user.id).

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 does not validate qty or sku. A non-numeric qty (a string like 'abc', or a missing value) makes Math.floor(NaN) = NaN. Math.max(1, NaN) is also NaN, so total becomes NaN. Infinity qty gives an Infinity total. Whether this lets an attacker bypass or zero the charge depends on how req.payments.charge treats NaN or Infinity, so it is a plausible finding rather than a confirmed one. An unknown sku could also return an undefined or NaN price, with the same effect.

trace.note: Iterates attacker-supplied items; items is not checked to be an array or non-empty
Catalog price looked up by attacker-controlled sku; the result is not checked for undefined or NaN
Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) returns NaN for non-numeric qty, so total becomes NaN
Non-finite total passed to the payment charge

finding.guards_checked: The Math.max(1, ...) floor stops zero and negative qty, but it does not stop NaN. There is no Number.isFinite or Number.isInteger check, no upper bound on qty, and no total > 0 check. The implementation of req.payments.charge is outside this repo, so I could not confirm how it handles NaN.

verdict.guard_found: Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14 only floors qty at 1; no isFinite/isInteger, upper bound, array check, or total>0 check. No auth middleware is visible in this file, though req.user is used.
verdict.reason: Lines 12-16 match the claim (cart.js:14 yields NaN for a non-numeric qty and Infinity for an Infinity qty, with no validation), but whether this is exploitable depends on req.payments.charge and req.catalog.price, which are not in this repo. A JSON body also cannot carry a literal Infinity, and a numeric string like "1e999" would be the route to it.
